summary: This benchmark investigates whether adapting the final transformer block of Qwen2.5-1.5B using an imitation objective induces reliance on a transplanted frozen feed-forward network from Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B. The study conducts a rigorous, multi-condition ablation study with bootstrap confidence intervals and negative control baselines, demonstrating that initial compatibility exists but the imitation objective does not increase functional reliance on the graft.
strengths: Methodologically sound experimental design featuring six well-motivated control conditions (shuffled expert, general-purpose donor, direct affine map, FFN ablation, and intact host).
High level of technical precision regarding model architectures, layer indices, parameter counts, and training hyperparameters.
Transparent reporting of negative and null results, explicitly identifying why a host-reconstruction imitation objective lacks incentive to develop graft-specific capabilities.
Statistical rigor with paired 95% confidence intervals resampling source files and minibatch order seeds.
weaknesses: Evaluated across only three random minibatch seeds, limiting the statistical power to detect small effect sizes in training variability.
The imitation objective (matching the intact host's hidden state) conceptually disincentivizes reliance on donor-specific capabilities, as acknowledged by the author.
Evaluation is restricted to a narrow CPython panel and next-token perplexity rather than functional code execution or generation benchmarks (e.g., HumanEval, MBPP).
suggestions: Test task-specific fine-tuning on downstream coding tasks (such as pass@k on HumanEval) where the donor model outperforms the host, providing a true gradient signal for graft reliance.
Increase the number of minibatch order seeds from 3 to at least 5-10 to narrow confidence intervals on borderline contrasts.
Explore multi-layer adaptation or low-rank adaptation across multiple adjacent host layers rather than isolating training strictly to block 28.

claims.text: We moved the same 13,074,432-weight feed-forward network from Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B into block 27 of the 28-block Qwen2.5-1.5B base model.
claims.source: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct; Qwen2.5 architecture specifications (28 layers, 0.5B intermediate size 4864 * hidden size 896 * 3 = 13,074,432 parameters)

claims.text: Affine input and output maps fitted on training activations translated between the host's 1,536 values per token and the donor's 896.
claims.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12186 (Qwen2.5 architectural parameters: 1.5B hidden size = 1536, 0.5B hidden size = 896)

claims.text: Model stitching uses a learned interface to test whether representations from separately trained models can work together. [Bansal, Nakkiran and Barak, model stitching]
claims.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.07682 (Bansal, Nakkiran, Barak, 2021: 'Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations')

novelty_vs_existing.title: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies stitching concepts to modular cross-model FFN transplants in modern decoder-only LLMs and measures changes in downstream block reliance following host adaptation.

novelty_vs_existing.title: LLM Augmented LLMs: Expanding Capabilities through Composition
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses on fine-grained intra-block feed-forward graft substitution and host adaptation dynamics rather than external cross-attention composition.
